newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco willing to listen on tobacco.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco willing to listen on tobacco.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco unit general counsel Charles Blixt said Wednesday the company was willing to listen to "any reasonable proposals" aimed at ending face-offs with anti-tobacco forces.

Asked about a Wall Street Journal report of discussions between RJR and Philip Morris Cos Inc and tobacco suit plaintiffs on a $300 billion industry-wide legal settlement, Blixt said, "We're willing to listen to any reasonable proposals."
Blixt, speaking before the start of the RJR Nabisco's annual shareholder meeting, declined to make any comments on reported settlement talks.
"I can't get into specifics," Blixt said.

He also said the company felt no increasing pressure coming from an ongoing wrongful death trial in Florida against Reynolds, or the tobacco litigation settlement last month involving Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett unit.
